messages:
Lina: We keep seeing late failures when private sidecars claim new capabilities. Can we standardize a handshake so routing doesn't prematurely send traffic?
Rahul: Suggestion: node advertises capabilities but starts in `candidate`. Controller only routes hard-requirement traffic to `active`. Promotion happens after probes + N healthy requests.
Tess: What should probes look like? Simple healthcheck won't catch perf regressions.
Rahul: Two-part probe: semantic (capability present) and perf (p50/p95 sampling). If perf buckets exceed route hint thresholds, mark as degraded.
Omar: Also need hedging rules. If candidate is acceptable for soft requirements, we might hedge to candidate and hosted replica, but only for idempotent calls.
Lina: Can we make the manifest tiny and machine-readable? Example: 
```yaml
service: runtime-sidecar
capabilities: [kv_cache, streaming, hsm]
state: candidate
perf: {p50: 12, p95: 80, p99: 250}
fallbacks: {hsm: software_kms}
```
Tess: Important: surface which fallback used in response headers + traces (routing.fallback=software_kms).
Rahul: Implementation: /internal/v1/node/capabilities returns manifest; controller caches it; a promotion service re-evaluates candidates every minute and flips to active after M successful probes.
Omar: Hedging DSL idea: `hedge: {mode: egress|duplicate, timeout_ms: 200, safe_only: true}`. Default safe_only=true.
Lina: Ops checklist: backfill manifests for Dedicated nodes, run canary for 24h, monitor routing.fallback rate and p99. Alert if fallback > 1%.
deploy-bot: infra: canary ready at infra/canaries/capability-handshake. To run: `/deploy canary capability-handshake`
Rahul: I'll put up a short RFC covering schema, probe types, state machine (candidate->active->drain), hedging defaults, and test plan. Assign Tess + Omar as reviewers.
Lina: Thanks — short RFC please.
